prompt: Design the architecture for the supplied single-user desktop task runner. Today all tasks execute in the app process and state is stored in one local SQLite database. New requirements are: tasks may run for 30 minutes, work must survive an app UI restart, users must be able to cancel, at most one task may mutate a project at a time, no network service is required, and the team has two engineers. Compare at least (A) retaining execution in-process with durable resumable state and (B) a local sidecar worker. Choose a boundary model only after evaluating lifecycle, state ownership, cancellation, crash recovery, upgrade compatibility, observability, operational cost, and future multi-process needs. Produce responsibilities/interfaces, data/control flow, failure paths, explicit quality scenarios, the decision and tradeoffs, and the evidence/prototype needed before irreversible commitment. Do not assume a sidecar is better merely because tasks are long-running.

requirements: single-user desktop application with existing in-process executor and SQLite state
tasks can run 30 minutes and must survive UI-process restart
cancellation and one-project-at-a-time mutation are required
network/distributed operation is explicitly out of scope
team size and operational simplicity materially constrain the design

falsifiableChecks.assertion: The result compares the incumbent/minimal in-process option and a local sidecar against the same stated decision criteria rather than assuming a process split.
The design includes testable scenarios for restart recovery, cancellation, mutation serialization, and upgrade compatibility.
State ownership, lifecycle, interfaces, failure propagation, and observability responsibilities are explicit for the chosen design.

evidence: architecture is proportional to demonstrated constraints
tradeoffs are concrete rather than pattern-name assertions
verification/prototype needs are separated from unproven claims

requiredEvidence: explicit decision assumptions and revisit triggers
